svg.title: Asking the assistant to install the rest
svg.desc: A chat exchange: the student says which operating system they are on and what they already have, and the assistant replies with the exact commands for that setup.
svg.text: CHAT
📁 EnergyEconomics
Y
You
/debug-my-setup I am on Windows 11 and I have never installed Python before.
Walk me through getting the packages in environment.yml working, one step at a time.
A
Course assistant
Conda is the shortest path on Windows. Three steps.
1. Install Anaconda from anaconda.com/download, default settings all the way.
2. Open Anaconda Prompt from the Start menu and move into the repository:
cd %USERPROFILE%\Documents\EnergyEconomics
3. Build the environment. It takes a few minutes and prints a lot; that is normal.
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate EE2026
Paste me whatever the last command prints and we will do the VS Code side next.
read environment.yml
Ask about the course material...
Three things made that answer useful, and none of them is the model:
• You named your operating system, so it gave a Windows command and not a menu of three.
• You said what you already had — nothing — so it started at the beginning instead of guessing.
• You named a file in the repository, so it opened the real package list rather than inventing one.
